thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p95 latency SLO breached in us-west for model-neo-mid. Automated routing fallback triggered 7x in the last 3m. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/metrics/alerts/2468017773

pagerduty-bot: Paging @maya-chen, @ethan-k (on-call). See PD-INC-4592.

maya-chen: taking it — joining

ethan-k: on my way, pulling up traces. initial impression: lots of reroutes between us-west and eu-west, and some sessions landed on neo-mid-q4 which has ~2x latency.

luca-r: I can see routing policy churn in the logs. there's a new rule that allows fallthrough to any 'compatible' variant; recent model onboarding added q4 as compatible.

priya-s: customer-side: ACME corp reported spike in latency and ~502 errors for some endpoints. They just pinged support.

maya-chen: quick mitigation — disabling auto-fallback for p95-triggered reroutes to stop the flip-flop. command:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://console/api/routing/policy/disable" -d '{"policy":"auto_fallback_p95","env":"prod"}'
```

ethan-k: running the command now...

ethan-k: output: { status: 200, message: "policy auto_fallback_p95 disabled" }

maya-chen: confirmed fallback disabled. seeing initial p95 decrease but routing still oscillating due to cached decisions. i'm applying a hysteresis increase to 90s to reduce thrash.

luca-r: hysteresis patch (applied to prod):
```json
{"policy":"routing_hysteresis","p95_window_s":90,"backoff_multiplier":1.5}
```

ops-bot: Change applied in canary, rolling to prod (change-id: ch-7892).

priya-s: marking customer impact: ACME had ~15% of requests above p95 during the spike window. will escalate to account team.

ethan-k: i recommend reverting the variant assignment from last deploy (deploy hash a1b2c3) — that made neo-mid-q4 visible to the compatibility matcher. initiating revert now.

maya-chen: revert executed, traffic should stop landing on q4 after current sessions drain (~60s). monitoring.

luca-r: dashboards: p95 trending down from ~2.5s to ~1.1s since changes. error rate stable. looks promising but continue to watch for 5m.

priya-s: customer update: ACME support says latency is improving, they'll keep us posted.

maya-chen: handing off on-call to @ethan-k for the rest of the window. i'm going to join the customer call and draft initial timeline.

ethan-k: taking oncall. quick notes:
- Root cause hypothesis: policy change allowed high-latency variant (neo-mid-q4) to be considered compatible, combined with aggressive p95-triggered reroutes and zero hysteresis -> route oscillation.
- Mitigations performed: disabled auto_fallback_p95, increased routing hysteresis to 90s, reverted variant mapping, rolled canary -> prod.
- Immediate next steps: monitor 30m, collect traces for sessions that hit q4, contact model-onboarding team to add latency metadata to variant registry.

incident-bot: Incident declared Sev2. Incident timeline doc: https://console.redwood/incidents/PD-INC-4592/timeline

maya-chen: thanks everyone. i'll spin up a postmortem draft and add the mitigation steps + suggested playbook changes (policy canaries + gating on variant latency).

ethan-k: noted. leaving handoff notes in the incident doc. will keep watching.

maya-chen: closing slack loop for now — please add any stray logs or traces as replies. :white_check_mark:
